name: Liga del Pacífico (fictional)
inspired_by: An old, wealthy Pacific-coast drug-trafficking federation of semi-independent factions (the type that grew from the mountain growing regions of north-west Mexico), now split by an internal succession war between rival factions, with heavy investment in synthetic-drug labs, armoured vehicles and drones. No real organisation, leader or faction name is used.

doctrine.summary: A trafficking federation whose armed wings are semi-autonomous 'cells' loyal to different faction bosses. Since the (fictional) succession split, the two halves fight each other street by street as well as fighting the state. Strengths: money, local informant networks ('halcones', lookouts with radios), armoured trucks and SUVs, .50-calibre rifles and growing use of commercial drones for surveillance and dropped explosives. Fighters range from well-paid veteran gunmen to poorly trained teenage recruits. It avoids open battle with the Army when it can, preferring roadblocks, ambushes on convoys and quick withdrawals into the mountains.
doctrine.fireteam: Cells of 6-12 gunmen in 2-4 vehicles, loosely paired; leaders carry radios; lookouts outside the fight.
tactics: Halcón lookouts and radio relays warn of approaching forces (map hazard: tripping a lookout alerts the area)
Roadblocks of burning vehicles to cut highways and slow pursuit
Ambush of convoys from high ground with .50-calibre rifles and belt-fed guns
Commercial drones for surveillance and dropped small explosives (game hazard)
Rapid withdrawal in armoured trucks into mountain hamlets and safe houses
Faction infighting: the player may find two cartel groups fighting each other

camo.name: MultiCam-style knock-off tactical kit
camo.use: Armed cells; often with home-made unit patches

grenadier: 40 mm underbarrel or standalone grenade launchers
at: .50 BMG anti-materiel rifle as the anti-vehicle weapon
squad_leader: AR-15 / M4-pattern rifle with optic, gold-trimmed pistol (status)

launchers: 40 mm grenade launchers [not_in_game as launcher class]

body_armor.notes: Commercial plate carriers, often with steel plates (spall risk) and cheap ballistic helmets; many low-level gunmen have none (game: mix of none and medium).

vehicles.notes: Home-armoured 'monster' trucks with welded plate, firing ports and turrets.
Commercially armoured full-size SUVs and pickups for bosses and hit squads, often stolen from or bought from civilian armouring shops.
Ordinary pickups carrying gunmen in the bed; often stolen.
Commercial quadcopters for surveillance and dropped explosives (game hazard).
Halcón lookouts and couriers on motorbikes.

unit_templates.name: Plaza defence (town held by the cartel)

support_assets: Halcón lookout network (early warning of player movement)
Commercial drones for surveillance and dropped explosives
Reinforcement trucks arriving from nearby safe houses
Burning-vehicle roadblocks that cut roads on the map

as_target: HVT capture of a cell or plaza boss
Hostage rescue from a safe house
Clear a cartel roadblock and reopen a highway

notes: FICTIONAL cartel; no real organisation, faction, leader or emblem is depicted. Inspired by the real-world type of an old Pacific-coast trafficking federation torn by an internal succession war (the 2024-2026 internal cartel war in north-west Mexico is the real-world reference for the infighting and drone use). Tone is game-level only: roadblocks, armoured trucks, drones, ambushes; no real operational detail. Hostile to the player, never hires or sells. At war with cartel_jalisco_nueva over trafficking routes, and with the Mexican state. Civilians are everywhere in cartel towns; the casualty penalties apply in full and many 'civilians' are lookouts (radio in hand), which should be a readable cue, never a guess.
proposed: unit_templates (roles lookout, drone_operator and driver are game roles)
